name: Rogue
bio: Power-absorbing mutant raised by Mystique as a Brotherhood operative; defected to the X-Men in Uncanny X-Men #171 (1983). For decades her power made touch itself dangerous, which turned every romance she had into a problem of intimacy.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: 90s / Blue-Gold
era.description: Jim Lee's X-Men relaunch through the Onslaught and Apocalypse: The Twelve era. Rogue and Gambit, the Blue and Gold teams, Age of Apocalypse.

relationships.label: The 90s' great slow burn
relationships.summary: A romance built on Rogue being unable to touch anyone and Gambit being unable to be honest with anyone. Spanned betrayals (his Marauders past, the Antarctica abandonment in Uncanny X-Men #350), separations, and the 2018 wedding; still married on Krakoa and after.

events.note: Rogue abandons Gambit in Antarctica after his Mutant Massacre role is revealed.

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: Foster mother and daughter
relationships.summary: Mystique and Destiny raised Rogue after her powers manifested, then used her as a Brotherhood weapon. Rogue's defection to the X-Men was a betrayal from Mystique's side and an escape from Rogue's; the two have spent decades alternating between manipulation and genuine care.

events.note: Rogue debuts as Mystique's protégé, absorbing Ms. Marvel's powers permanently.
Rogue asks Xavier for help and joins the X-Men.
Rogue gains control of her power; Mystique's manipulations in the surrounding arc resurface.

source.name: Magneto
source.real_name: Max Eisenhardt (long known as Erik Lehnsherr)

continuity.name: Earth-616
continuity.description: The main Marvel Comics continuity, running continuously since Fantastic Four #1 (1961).

era.name: Claremont Era
era.description: Giant-Size X-Men #1 (1975) through Chris Claremont's departure after X-Men #3 (1991). The all-new team, Phoenix, Days of Future Past, the Brood, Inferno.

relationships.label: Savage Land interlude
relationships.summary: A brief, deliberate romance in the Savage Land that Claremont wrote as two outsiders recognising each other. It mattered mostly for what it set up: Rogue's enduring sympathy for Magneto and the alternate-universe marriage in the Age of Apocalypse.

events.note: Rogue and Magneto, depowered and stranded, become close.
Magneto executes Zaladane; Rogue cannot follow him.

source.name: Magneto
source.real_name: Max Eisenhardt (long known as Erik Lehnsherr)

continuity.name: Earth-295 (Age of Apocalypse)
continuity.description: Alternate timeline in which Xavier died before founding the X-Men and Apocalypse conquered North America. Age of Apocalypse crossover (1995).

era.name: 90s / Blue-Gold
era.description: Jim Lee's X-Men relaunch through the Onslaught and Apocalypse: The Twelve era. Rogue and Gambit, the Blue and Gold teams, Age of Apocalypse.

relationships.label: Married, with a son
relationships.summary: In the Age of Apocalypse, where Xavier died before founding the X-Men, Magneto leads the team and is married to Rogue; their son is Charles. The pairing is the clearest example of the database's premise: the same two characters, a different continuity, a different relationship.

events.note: Magneto and Rogue shown as husband and wife.
